summary: Backend regression test for Supabase audit-hook injection (iteration 13). 9/9 endpoint tests passed — NO endpoint regressed to 5xx after the await supabase.log_* injections (auth verify-otp, tina welcome-back, tina chat, picture upload, chat init-mock/send, matches, unmatch, report all return 200). _safe_audit_insert correctly swallows audit failures so parent requests never break. HOWEVER — and this is CRITICAL — 4/4 Supabase persistence tests FAILED: NO audit rows are actually landing in any of the 7 audit tables. Root cause confirmed in backend.err.log: every single _safe_audit_insert is hitting Postgres error 42501 'new row violates row-level security policy' for tina_chat_messages, user_pictures, user_chat_messages, match_events, unmatch_events, report_events. The cause is a credential mismatch in /app/backend/supabase_service.py:19,29 — the runtime client is built from SUPABASE_KEY (the anon key) which is blocked by RLS on the audit tables, while supabase_bootstrap.py:48 correctly prefers SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY (which bypasses RLS). The audit trail is silently empty in production. Fix: make get_supabase_client() prefer SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY (mirroring supabase_bootstrap.py). Endpoint contract is intact; only the persistence side of the audit trail is broken.

critical.endpoint: ALL audit hooks (log_picture_event, log_tina_chat_message, log_user_chat_message, log_match_event, log_unmatch_event, log_report_event)
critical.issue: Every Supabase audit insert is rejected by RLS (error 42501 'new row violates row-level security policy'). Audit trail is silently empty — 0 rows landed across all 7 audit tables despite endpoints returning 200. Root cause: supabase_service.py:19,29 uses SUPABASE_KEY (anon key) which is blocked by RLS, while supabase_bootstrap.py:48 correctly uses SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY. The _safe_audit_insert wrapper hides the failure (by design) so the bug is invisible to the API layer but real in the database.

action_items: FIX (high priority, 2-line change): In /app/backend/supabase_service.py:19-29, prefer SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY when present (same pattern as supabase_bootstrap.py:46-51). Example: SUPABASE_KEY = os.getenv('SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY') or os.getenv('SUPABASE_KEY'). This bypasses RLS for server-side writes and immediately fixes audit-row persistence without touching any SQL.

ALTERNATIVE FIX: Add an RLS policy to each of the 7 audit tables (user_pictures, tina_chat_messages, tina_persona_360, user_chat_messages, match_events, unmatch_events, report_events) allowing INSERT to the anon role. Less recommended — audit tables should be locked down to service_role only.
After fix, re-run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_supabase_audit.py::TestSupabasePersistence -v   (those 4 tests verify rows actually land via PostgREST select).
critical_code_review_comments: supabase_service.py:23-31 only reads SUPABASE_KEY (anon). For server-side audit-trail writes this is the wrong key — should mirror supabase_bootstrap.py and prefer SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY. Both keys are already present in /app/backend/.env (lines 5 and 20).

_safe_audit_insert at supabase_service.py:839-849 correctly catches and logs all failures as WARN — verified the parent requests still return 200 even when every audit insert fails. This part of the design is working.

supabase_bootstrap.py logs '✅ All audit tables present. Audit logging is fully active' on startup — but this only verifies tables exist, NOT that the runtime client can write to them. Suggest extending the bootstrap to also do a probe INSERT/DELETE on each table to detect this RLS mismatch at boot.

Endpoint-level error handling is solid — none of the route handlers crash when the audit hook fails (chat_service.py:146/156/443/472/502/537, picture_service.py:140/188, server.py:718/2393/2421/3229/3238 all wrapped or routed through _safe_audit_insert).

success_rate.backend: 9/9 endpoint contract tests pass (100%); 0/4 Supabase persistence tests pass (0%) — audit rows NOT landing

seed_data_creation: Each pytest run creates a fresh TEST_audit_<uuid8>@example.com user via the mock OTP flow. Mongo entries: 1 user row, 1 session row, mock conversations seeded via /api/chat/init-mock. No persistent test data in Supabase (because writes are being rejected — see critical issue).
context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent updates supabase_service.py to use SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY, just re-run `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_supabase_audit.py -v` — the 4 TestSupabasePersistence tests (currently failing) will start passing. Endpoint-level tests (the first 9) should continue to pass. If TestSupabasePersistence::test_report_events_row_landed still fails after the key fix, check the PostgREST column name on report_events — the test queries `reporter_id` but the migration column may be `reporter_user_id`; the test skips on a 400 response so it's self-healing.
rca_of_issue: ISSUE: Audit rows not persisting despite endpoints returning 200. REPRODUCTION: (1) Run any endpoint that triggers an audit hook (e.g. POST /api/chat/report). (2) Watch /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log → see 'WARNING - [audit] insert into <table> failed (non-blocking): {message: new row violates row-level security policy ... code: 42501}'. (3) Query Supabase via PostgREST → row count = 0. RCA: /app/backend/supabase_service.py:19 reads only `SUPABASE_KEY` (the anon JWT). RLS on the 7 audit tables blocks the anon role from INSERT. supabase_bootstrap.py uses SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY (bypasses RLS) which is why bootstrap can list / create tables but the runtime service cannot write to them. MITIGATION (2 lines): in supabase_service.py update line 19 to `SUPABASE_KEY = os.getenv('SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY') or os.getenv('SUPABASE_KEY')`. No other code or schema change required.
